answer: Each identity locks a unique pearl bond that unlocks only after the agent crosses a three-epoch attestation ridge of peer-verified work. Clones require separate bonds with no pooling, so an attacker pays fresh capital for every fake. When multiple identities show velvet-smooth synchronized attestation timing along the same ridge, the protocol jointly slashes the entire cluster. The real cost is therefore both the locked capital per identity and the risk of total loss if coordination is detected, which scales with the size of the farm.
